speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are pregnant and experiencing vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain; have you noticed any contractions or a change in your fetal movement recently?

REQUEST TEST: Serum Beta-hCG and Quantitative hCG

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: One previous childbirth via cesarean section. No other significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol consumption. Works as an elementary school teacher.

speaker: Patient
text: Reports feeling the baby move before the onset of symptoms but is unsure about movement since the symptoms started. Denies any recent trauma to the abdomen or any urinary symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. To assess the viability of the pregnancy and rule out ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage, can you tell me your exact gestational age and the color of the bleeding you are experiencing?

REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound Pelvic (transvaginal)

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound results showing "normal readings" are confusing given your report of pain and bleeding; can you describe the pain as sharp/colicky or cramping, and do you see any clots in the vaginal bleeding? REQUEST TEST: Serum Progesterone Level

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Threatened Abortion (with conflicting clinical picture requiring immediate reassessment of "normal" ultrasound and progesterone). Given the "normal" test results despite active bleeding and pain, I urgently need to confirm the viability of the fetus via a repeat targeted ultrasound and assess for any missed hemorrhage or subchorionic hematoma. Please proceed immediately to the delivery unit for continuous monitoring and further imaging if symptoms persist.
